label: the danda, and the full stop that has largely replaced it
note: Every headword in the corpus punctuates with a full stop, which is what Marathi does now, and a candidate who had never seen a danda met it on the first authentic notice. MR-W64-danda closes it at chapter 64. It is the FIRST MARK IN THE TRACK TAUGHT FOR RECOGNITION RATHER THAN PRODUCTION -- the reader keeps writing the full stop and learns to read the upright stroke in poetry, older printing and signs nobody has reset -- and the lesson names that distinction because it recurs.
